source.quote: Grace Design's own page for the m900, read 2026-11-25. « USB supported sample rates »: « 44.1, 48, 88.2, 96, 176.4, 192, 352.8, 384kHz ». Features: « Asynchronous USB interface for jitter free computer audio playback, supports up to 384kHz PCM and 256x DSD »; « USB, S/PDIF and Toslink digital inputs, supports up to 192kHz (Toslink up to 96kHz) »; « 4 different DAC filter settings to tailor playback performance to personal preference ». Converter: « The m900 DAC uses the latest generation AKM 4490 chip, which features 32-bit processing ». The spec table gives no bit depth. Measurements are taken at the analogue output rather than for the D/A path alone: « THD+N at Maximum Volume, 1kHz, 22Hz-22kHz BW » with « @1.0V out, no load <0.002% », and « Dynamic Range ... 20-22kHz bandwidth 112 dB » / « 115 dB » A-weighted. No DSD figure is given for S/PDIF or Toslink. No terms-of-use page exists on the site; the footer carries the ordinary copyright line.

facts.chip: « the latest generation AKM 4490 chip, which features 32-bit processing ».

device_settings.why: « 4 different DAC filter settings to tailor playback performance to personal preference ». A count and no names - the ninth maker in three days to do it. No value can be recorded. The AK4490's own filter menu is well known to have names; this page does not give them.

_une_phrase_qui_note_TROIS_entrees_a_la_: « USB, S/PDIF and Toslink digital inputs, supports up to 192kHz (Toslink up to 96kHz) » - and the USB row elsewhere says 384 kHz. So the 192 is the S/PDIF figure, the parenthesis gives optical its own, and USB is covered by its own table. One sentence, three ceilings, and only the parenthesis stops it from being read as a single limit. Same economy as Pro-Ject's « 192 kHz (coaxial only) », and the same hazard for an automated read.
